label: late original-phase input of w/t/m/2/0/z/i/b/g
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98% of activation mass); it never fires at t=0 and is rare at t<3. Its firing rate climbs with position (orig_idx 8 fires 35% of the time against 1% at idx 1), so longer sequences carry more of it. The input token sets the level: w is by far the strongest (28% rate, a quarter of the mass, and it is the top token in every max example, including repeated w w w), followed by t, m, 2, 0, z, then i, b, g. First occurrences fire more than repeats, but w still fires when repeated. Activity barely continues into the delimiter and copy phases, apart from a weak blip at recall_idx 1. It is not a clean token detector: other tokens (o, u, k, a, s, ...) also fire late in some sequences, and listed tokens often stay silent, so there seems to be a history-dependent accumulated component (sequences beginning with v/x/f/h fire somewhat more) that the predicate does not capture. Dev F1 is about 0.57 and mass recall 0.75.
